description: Fetch the short article summary that answers "what is X?". The extract is a truncated fragment from the start of the lead section — usually a sentence or two, and as little as a tenth of the lead — alongside the Wikidata QID (wikibase_item) for cross-referencing with wikidata-mcp-server, a short description, a thumbnail URL, the canonical article URL, the revision the extract was read from, and, for a geotagged article, latitude and longitude that pass straight to wikipedia_search_nearby to answer "what else is notable near this". For the lead section in full, call wikipedia_get_article with section_index 0. Redirects are followed and reported in redirected_from, and in redirect_section when the alias points into a section; the extract still covers the whole article. When page_type is "disambiguation", the title matched a disambiguation page — call wikipedia_search_articles with a more specific query to find the intended article. Prefer this over wikipedia_get_article unless article depth is needed.

title.description: Article title (URL-decoded), e.g. "Python (programming language)". A trailing #fragment is accepted and ignored; the characters < > [ ] { } and | cannot appear in a Wikipedia page name. Special: and Media: titles, and interwiki links such as "wikt:cat", name no page.

name: wikipedia_get_summary

description.description: Short description of the article subject.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: No Wikipedia article exists for the given title. `invalid_title`: The title can name no page: it contains characters MediaWiki forbids in a page name, is a Special: or Media: title in any edition's spelling, or is an interwiki link such as "wikt:cat". `invalid_language`: The language is not a valid BCP 47 code, or names a Wikipedia edition that does not exist. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

extract.description: Plain-text summary extract — a truncated fragment from the start of the lead section, not the whole lead. Superscripts and subscripts stay apart from the text beside them (10²³, H₂O), as wikipedia_get_article renders them. Call wikipedia_get_article with section_index 0 for the full lead.

last_modified.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of that revision, for dating the content.

latitude.description: WGS 84 latitude of the article subject in decimal degrees. Pass with longitude to wikipedia_search_nearby, whose inputs carry these names, to find other notable articles around the same point. Absent for an article that is not geotagged.

longitude.description: WGS 84 longitude of the article subject in decimal degrees. Pass with latitude to wikipedia_search_nearby, whose inputs carry these names, to find other notable articles around the same point. Absent for an article that is not geotagged.

notice.description: Guidance when the page has no summary extract, when the title redirects into a section (naming its section_index once the table of contents confirms it), or when the redirect could not be checked.

page_type.description: Page type from the Wikipedia REST API: "standard" (an article, including one whose lead yields no extract), "disambiguation" (a disambiguation page — call wikipedia_search_articles with a more specific query), "mainpage" (the edition's Main Page), or "no-extract" (a page outside the article namespace, such as a category, or with non-wikitext content).

pageid.description: Wikipedia page ID. Absent when the API omits it.

redirect_section.description: Section of the article the alias points into — its heading when the table of contents confirms it, otherwise the alias's raw fragment. The extract still summarizes the whole article; a notice gives the section_index to read when it is confirmed.

redirected_from.description: Original alias followed to the resolved article. Absent when the title is not a redirect, or when the redirect could not be checked (a notice then says so).

revision_id.description: ID of the revision the extract was read from. "https://<edition>.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=<revision_id>" is a permanent link to exactly that version.

thumbnail_url.description: URL of the article thumbnail image, if available.

title.description: Resolved article title (may differ from input for redirects).

url.description: Canonical desktop URL of the article (e.g. "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eiffel_Tower"), for citing the page rather than composing a URL from the title.

wikibase_item.description: Wikidata QID (e.g. "Q28865"). Use to chain into wikidata-mcp-server without a separate lookup.

title: Get Wikipedia Summary
